text:
maria (support): forwarding a customer report — after the canary rollout yesterday they see instructions lost and the system prompt truncated in long conversations. customer says it started immediately after canary c-2026-04-12 went to 20% in eu-west-1. attaching repro and logs below.

maria (support): REPRO (redacted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \ \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \ \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.3-canary","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant. Follow these instructions exactly: 1) ALWAYS prefix outputs with [ACME] 2) When uncertain, ask clarifying qns. 3) Keep JSON outputs minimal."},{"role":"user","content":"Long conversation continues... (history ~15k tokens) \n... final user prompt: Summarize the plan."}],"max_output_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```

maria (support): Observed response from canary model: system instruction missing/prefixed part truncated, assistant stopped being consistent with [ACME] prefix and produced free-form text. Customer included full history and says truncation point around token ~12050.

raj (ml-eng): Can you paste the exact model id and canary tag? also which container hash?

maria (support): model: redwood-v2.3-canary (canary c-2026-04-12), container: r-infer:v2.3-canary@sha256:8f9c. Canary percent = 20% in eu-west-1 only. Customer region = eu-west-1.

jordan (oncall): digging into router logs for that timeframe, saw a few 5xx's but mostly OK. however I see repeated log line: \"kv_cache_eviction: policy=GREEDY evicted_prefix_tokens=1024 at seq=12080\" — looks like prefix eviction triggered.

raj (ml-eng): that eviction line is interesting. we changed some kernel selection and prefix handling in the canary to optimize KV memory. possible off-by-one in eviction threshold. cc @ben so product is aware.

maria (support): customer provided snippet of returned content and token counts: 
```
last_client_token_index: 12049
server_received_tokens: 12050
prefix_evicted: true
assistant_response_excerpt: \"...then we should proceed.\" (missing the mandatory [ACME] prefix)
```

ben (product): any quick mitigation we can offer the customer while we root cause? revert canary for that customer or pin them to stable model?

raj (ml-eng): immediate options: 1) pin the customer to redwood-v2.2-stable (no change to prefix logic), 2) increase per-request max_sequence_limit (if supported) so eviction doesn't trigger, or 3) roll back the canary at region level. We should reproduce locally with same long-history.

maria (support): customer wants repro steps so they can test themselves; sharing a condensed payload that reproduces locally (we verified).

maria (support): MINIMAL REPRO that reproduced for us: a system prompt ~3.5k tokens, then a repeated filler series to push history to ~12k tokens, final user prompt requesting structured output. We get missing prefix consistently when canary used.

raj (ml-eng): I pulled the canary diffs — tokenizer preprocessor commit abc1234 changed trimming semantics around leading system whitespace and a change in eviction threshold in infer runtime commit f1e2d3. The tokenizer change could shift token counts so eviction happens earlier. Working theory: tokenization delta + lowered eviction buffer -> prefix falls out of KV cache mid-request.

jordan (oncall): posted relevant router trace snippet: 
```
[2026-04-12T09:14:27Z] request_id=uuid-xyz route=eu-west-1 target=redwood-v2.3-canary seq_len=12080 kv_eviction=true evicted_tokens=1024 kernel=opt-attn-v2
```

raj (ml-eng): i'll run a local compare: tokenize(customer_history) against stable and canary to confirm tokenization shift and measure where eviction would trigger.

ben (product): we should also prepare a short customer note: acknowledge regression, provide temporary workarounds (pin to stable or request smaller history), and ETA for fix once root cause validated.

maria (support): customer prefers a rollback in-region if that's fastest. can we do that now?

deploy-bot: Canary c-2026-04-12 status: running @ 20% in eu-west-1. To rollback run: `deploy rollback --canary c-2026-04-12 --region eu-west-1` (requires deploy approvals).

raj (ml-eng): i'm 80% confident it's the tokenizer preproc commit. quick fix options: revert tokenizer commit (low risk) or bump eviction buffer in runtime (requires new build). Revert + quick canary redeploy is fastest.

jordan (oncall): if we rollback canary now, we should monitor for 1 hour and ask customer to verify. I'll prepare a monitor for prefix-presence metric and token-eviction rate.

maria (support): customer asked for an ETA. suggested messaging: we identified a likely root cause related to tokenization and prefix eviction; we can rollback the canary in your region within ~30-45m and will confirm after monitoring.

raj (ml-eng): started local reproducer, comparing token counts: stable -> 12050 tokens; canary -> tokenized length increased by +18 tokens on same text, enough to cross eviction boundary in several cases. Confirmed.

ben (product): approved rollback for eu-west-1 only. lodging rollback request now.

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered for c-2026-04-12 in eu-west-1 by ben. ETA ~15m.

maria (support): told customer rollback underway, asked them not to change traffic.

jordan (oncall): rollback completed at 1976300800. monitors show evicted_prefix_tokens rate returning to baseline.

maria (support): customer verified after rollback: system instruction present, [ACME] prefix restored in subsequent responses. customer marks as "working for now".

raj (ml-eng): follow-up actions: 1) revert tokenizer commit in canary branch + add tokenization diff tests for long-system-prompts, 2) add guardrail in runtime to never evict system prompt tokens (preserve_system_prefix flag), 3) instrument prefix-presence metric.

ben (product): i'll draft the customer note and coordinate a delayed full canary (with fixes) and postmortem.

maria (support): closing loop — customer satisfied with rollback for now. will re-open if regression returns. :white_check_mark:
